subject: Azure/GCP private offer — reseller pass-through, tiered commit & invoicing flow
messages:

Subject: Private offer question — reseller pass-through and tiered commit (CloudOps)

Hi Tessa / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're excited to move forward with a private offer on Azure and GCP but have a couple of asks before we can pull the PO:

- We work through a reseller (Nimbus Partners). Nimbus needs to invoice us and then they will pay Redwood via the marketplace. Can you confirm whether Redwood can pass the marketplace discount through to Nimbus (so our commercial discount is reflected in their invoice) or whether Nimbus will receive commissions on top of a list-price billing pattern?
- We need a tiered-commit structure that gives us an uplifted discount at 100k / 250k / 500k USD ARR buckets across both clouds. How would that map in a single private offer versus separate private offers per cloud?
- Billing cadence: our procurement team requires monthly invoices that show the committed discount applied and a detailed unit breakdown for audit. Is that doable?

I've attached our initial SOW and a rough usage estimate. Can you share a sample pricing matrix and an outline of how commissions to Nimbus would be handled?

Thanks —
Maya Patel
Head of Procurement, CloudOps, Inc.
maya.patel@cloudops.com
+1 415 555 0198

Attachment: CloudOps_SOW_v1.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@cloudops.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — reseller pass-through and tiered commit (CloudOps)

Hi Maya — great to hear you're ready to move. Short answers up front, details below and a pricing matrix attached.

- Pass-through / reseller: We can structure the private offer so Nimbus sees the net effective price (marketplace list minus private discount) in their billing flow; operationally this is done via the reseller pass-through configuration and a partner margin waterfall. Nimbus will receive commission based on the agreed channel margin table, not a separate add-on on top of the discounted price.
- Tiered commits: We typically implement tiered discounts as milestones in a single private offer with ranges per cloud. That lets you keep one contract while allowing Azure and GCP SKUs to have separate effective rates. If you prefer separate private offers per cloud (for legal/PO reasons) we can mirror the exact tier structure.
- Billing cadence: Monthly invoices with line-item usage and applied discount are standard for dedicated/reserved contracts; for marketplace private offers we can provide a monthly statement export that meets audit requirements.

I've attached a proposed_pricing_matrix.xlsx with three scenarios: unified private offer (preferred), separate per-cloud private offers, and a reseller-commission waterfall with suggested margins for Nimbus. A couple of notes:
- We recommend a Nimbus margin range of 10–18% depending on commit tier and whether they take onboarding services.
- For Azure there is a small marketplace fee that reduces marginally the net passed through to Nimbus; GCP is more straightforward.

Can we schedule a 30-min alignment with your finance + Nimbus next week to finalize the waterfall and PO format? Suggested times: Tue 4/27 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 4/28 13:00–14:00 PT.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Strategic Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: proposed_pricing_matrix.xlsx

Maya — quick follow up from product/ops side. A few practicals so your procurement team has clear language for the PO and Nimbus has what they need for invoicing:

1) Private offer setup: we'll need Nimbus' marketplace merchant ID and legal entity doc to map the pass-through. Once we have that we can produce a draft private offer that lists the effective net price for each SKU and the partner split.
2) Commission timing: payouts to Nimbus are monthly, 30 days after invoice reconciliation. We include commission as a separate line on partner remittance statements; it does not change the customer's invoice amount.
3) Contract: we can support a single Redwood quote that references both Azure and GCP SKUs and includes the tiered thresholds. Procurement-friendly language: "Customer commits to X USD ARR across Azure and GCP in exchange for the discounts in Appendix A. Partner commissions are paid by Redwood per the channel waterfall and do not adjust the Customer-facing invoice."

I'll join the alignment call and bring our marketplace operations lead.

—Aditya

Thanks all — calendar invite sent for Tue 4/27 10:00 PT. Per Maya's asks I've attached two items: a sample invoice template and a draft quote/DocuSign packet. Key callouts:

- Invoice template (attached) includes monthly line item usage, applied private discount, and a reconciliation section for true-ups.
- Termination/true-up: draft language in the quote defines a 90-day true-up window after each 12-month period; if annualized consumption falls under the committed floor by more than 15% we apply a one-time true-up equal to the delta at the committed rate.
